lxc_6a00983dca93a0a4.text: Understand tennis rallies, safe and risky shots, court surfaces, and four famous tournament examples.

lxc_bb0d8dff59c60552.text: Tennis is not only hitting the ball hard.

lxc_9f43eac72a320dfc.text: This lesson shows one clear idea: players make smart choices inside a rally.

lxc_609bf075be3714d9.text: You will learn what a rally is, why some shots are safe or risky, and how clay, grass, and hard courts can change the match.

lxc_bb44fe2ac22293da.text: A tennis point starts with a serve.

lxc_4ff8ebbcde372ddf.text: The other player tries to return the ball.

lxc_1fa488d60b7693e5.text: If both players keep hitting the ball over the net and inside the court, they are in a rally.

lxc_4c72b99fc3fa8fb9.text: A rally is like a small conversation with the ball.

lxc_9233661f22be5e20.text: One player hits deep to push the other player back.

lxc_23e11fae92e19e24.text: The next player may return safely to stay in the point.

lxc_79a00c871494a2bb.text: Then someone may see open space and attack.

lxc_48585abe46146f50.text: A safe shot gives the player more room for error.

lxc_e8fe0fbce5457722.text: It often goes higher over the net or deeper into the court.

lxc_3bb0b38fcdbea3fb.text: A deep safe shot can make the opponent move back and wait.

lxc_f76dd787f6685974.text: A risky shot tries to finish the point faster.

lxc_07549fc0b7b98d00.text: It may go close to a line, close to the net, or into a small open space.

lxc_a8f9dfefe3e967a8.text: If it works, the player may win the point.

lxc_8d399479c00d15ba.text: If it misses, the point is over.

lxc_c93dcf74ad5a0869.text: Good tennis players do not attack every ball.

lxc_6078edcf1cebba7a.text: They ask a quick question: Is this a good moment to stay safe, or is this the moment to take a risk?

lxc_c6a684ffecaf1433.text: Tennis is played on different court surfaces.

lxc_46d9a34a43eae35e.text: The main three are clay, grass, and hard court.

lxc_ade41f9ca120149c.text: The surface changes how the ball bounces and how fast a point can feel.

lxc_6ecabea6f0b078c2.text: Clay often makes the ball slower and higher after the bounce.

lxc_3a98dd2bef38a870.text: This can make rallies longer, so patience matters.

lxc_febbc25a4088c504.text: Grass often makes the ball stay lower and move faster, so quick reactions matter.

lxc_5898ed64338e14da.text: Hard courts are often more balanced, so many styles can work.

lxc_c404f64c09bab387.text: The same player may need a different plan on each surface.

lxc_c16a450380a3e12d.text: On clay, one more patient shot may be smart.

lxc_f63c489b0235ceb8.text: On grass, a fast first move may be important.

lxc_36617090a8f3815e.text: On a hard court, balance and timing can matter a lot.

lxc_5bb65c3807522ee1.text: The four Grand Slam tournaments show different tennis tests.

lxc_1763192de2476e9a.text: The Australian Open is on hard courts in Melbourne.

lxc_e853876d4be94364.text: Roland-Garros, also called the French Open, is on clay in Paris.

lxc_39d4b3e48cb7394f.text: Wimbledon is on grass in London.

lxc_54dd6718ee9f024d.text: The US Open is on hard courts in New York.

lxc_3a2de5bcf858cb92.text: These names are not only sports trivia.

lxc_42a67b029682e992.text: They show why a player needs more than one plan.

lxc_7ef5d5d60320b90e.text: On grass, quick reactions can help.

lxc_de330b9c64d39465.text: On hard courts, timing and balance can help.

lxc_3f3e0a4860f1030d.text: Tennis is simple to start: serve, return, and keep the ball in.

lxc_cb853a01b799ca0d.text: But inside that simple rule, players solve many small problems.

lxc_986723e52985ed31.text: A risky shot can finish the point.

lxc_3448ff83b422222d.text: A court surface can change the whole plan.
